sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Close Grip Push Up is a bodyweight pressing exercise that targets the triceps with secondary emphasis on the chest and shoulders.

By placing the hands directly under the shoulders with thumbs and index fingers forming a triangle, the elbows track close to the body and load the triceps more than a standard push-up.

It is a portable, equipment-free exercise that builds upper-body pressing strength and elbow lockout power.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Directly targets the triceps brachii
- Strengthens chest and anterior shoulders
- Reinforces core and full-body bracing
- Requires no equipment and minimal space
- Easily scaled by elevating the hands or dropping to the knees
- Improves elbow lockout strength carry-over to bench press
- Builds shoulder stability and scapular control

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Triceps Brachii

Secondary: Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoids, Core, Serratus Anterior

sections.heading: Set Up
sections.content:
1. Begin in a plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders.
2. Bring the hands closer together so the thumbs and index fingers form a triangle.
3. Brace the core and squeeze the glutes for a straight body line.

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Arms fully extended with shoulders directly over the wrists.
2. Body in a straight line from head to heels.
3. Gaze slightly forward of the hands; neck neutral.

sections.heading: Lower
sections.content:
1. Bend the elbows to lower the body toward the ground.
2. Keep the elbows close to the sides as you descend.
3. Lower until the chest nearly touches the floor.

sections.heading: Press and Repeat
sections.content:
1. Push the body back up by extending the elbows.
2. Drive through the palms and engage the triceps and chest.
3. Return to the starting position and repeat for the desired reps.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Flaring the elbows out wide
- Letting the hips sag or pike up
- Failing to descend through the full range of motion
- Allowing the head to drop or jut forward
- Placing the hands too far forward or back
- Holding the breath through the rep
- Losing core bracing and twisting through the torso

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Flat, non-slip floor surface
- Optional: Exercise mat for hand and knee comfort
- Optional: Push-up handles or parallettes for wrist relief
- Optional: Mirror to monitor form

sections.heading: Hand Position
sections.content:
1. Place the hands directly under the shoulders.
2. Bring the hands together so the thumbs and index fingers form a triangle.
3. Spread the fingers wide and press evenly through the palms.
4. Keep the wrists stacked under the shoulders.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Feet hip-width apart, toes on the floor.
2. Torso: Straight line from head to heels, glutes and core engaged.
3. Arms: Elbows tucked close to the ribs, not flared.
4. Shoulders: Packed, away from the ears.
5. Head: Neutral, eyes slightly forward of the hands.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Standard Push-Up: Wider hand position emphasizing chest
- Diamond Push-Up: Hands together with thumbs touching
- Tricep Dips on Bench: Bodyweight triceps isolation
- Close-Grip Bench Press: Loaded barbell variation
- Tricep Pushdown: Cable-based triceps isolation
- Skull Crusher: Lying tricep extension

sections.heading: Close Grip Push Up Variations
sections.content:
Knee Close Grip Push Up: Easier variation on the knees
Incline Close Grip Push Up: Hands elevated for less load
Decline Close Grip Push Up: Feet elevated for greater load
Weighted Close Grip Push Up: Plate or vest for added resistance
Tempo Close Grip Push Up: Slow eccentric for hypertrophy
Pause Close Grip Push Up: Pause near the floor for greater triceps tension

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Wrist Pain: Use push-up handles or parallettes for a neutral grip
Elbow Pain: Reduce range of motion and lighten the load
Shoulder Issues: Keep the elbows tucked and shoulders packed
Low Strength: Drop to the knees or elevate the hands
Advanced: Elevate the feet or add a weighted vest
Beginners: Start with knee or incline variations to learn the pattern
